newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: SRI LANKA RUPEE ENDS STEADY ON HIGH DLR LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: SRI LANKA RUPEE ENDS STEADY ON HIGH DLR LIQUIDITY.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed stable against the dollar on Thursday despite import covering, as the market was well supplied with the U.S. unit, dealers said.
The rupee opened at 58.91 and closed at 58.92, they said.
"The market is very well supplied, with an inflow of nearly $70 million in the last three days from the sale of NDB (National Development Bank) shares," said a HongKong Bank dealer.
Last week the NDB made a foreign offer of 16.5 million shares, at 260 rupees each.
"About $60 million dollars would have been sold to the Central Bank in the last couple of days," said the Hongkong dealer.
The market has been well supplied with dollars during most months of this year, due to substantial inflows through the Colobo stock market, dealers said.
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by one local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.9050 and 60.0950.
Overnight call rates closed at 10 percent after opening at 11 and rising to 12, dealers said.
"The tight money market conditions of the last few days has eased, with banks selling dollars to the Central Bank," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
